auth_network_tag.note: ConfigParam 48 (AUTH policy) is mandatory and critical from global version 16, and a version-16 genesis needs an explicit public 256-bit network tag; tos assigns none. The value is SHA-256 of the ASCII rule, so anyone can recompute it. It changes every epoch: all epochs share global id 2, and Quantum wallet keys and signatures bind the tag, so a fresh tag keeps an epoch's wallets and signed messages from carrying over to the next, as the fresh-identity checks do for everything else. It is never a tos test namespace (one repeated byte, or bytes 00..1f) nor the mainnet admission candidate's 0x42 repeated. The genesis step refuses unless TOS_AUTH_NETWORK_TAG names exactly this value, and records it with the ConfigParam 48 cell hash in genesis.json. Chosen by the test lead on 2026-10-17 for epoch 4 and moved to epoch 5 on 2026-10-24 and to epoch 6 on 2026-10-28; the owner may replace the rule before the launch.

features.note: Neither may be activated on the public testnet until its own acceptance gate passes (memo public-testnet/README.md section 3.2). The shielded pool's gate passed for one bounded test on epoch 6 only (shielded_pool_record); Energy stays disabled.

shielded_pool_record.scope: PRI-01..03 on public testnet epoch 6 only, run by the test lead from three fresh test wallets (sender A 130, sender B 15, workchain-0 recipient 5 TOS; 150 TOS budget, no replenishment without a new approval). Not a mainnet activation and not a privacy product: sender, pool, recipient, amounts and timing stay public.
shielded_pool_record.metadata_only: This record neither deploys nor protects anything: the pool is an ordinary workchain-0 contract that needs no ConfigParam, capability vote, node rebuild or validator restart. Deployment and every send are separate journaled steps under the go points below.

pool.note: Frozen by tos tools/shielded-pool-circuit/crosscheck prepare_public_pool at the runtime commit from two independent checkouts and builds; code, data, StateInit and manifest were byte-identical. The address is the StateInit hash. The StateInit binds global id 2 through the execution domain, not the AUTH tag, so the same profile and key give the same address on every epoch (accepted limitation E5-13; a fresh pool refuses another pool's anchors with 152/153/154). Before deployment, read the address from two validators: it must be absent or uninitialized; after deployment, its code and data must hash to these values on both.
